result.title: Actionable Meta-Requirements for AI Robustness Auditing
result.summary: AI-enabled systems must remain dependable when the conditions under which they operate change (e.g., due to input perturbations, distribution shifts, or changes in external dependencies). This makes robustness auditing of such systems important for judging whether the available evidence is sufficient to support a defined robustness conclusion. However, designing an AI robustness auditing framework is challenging. A key unresolved issue is determining the requirements such a framework should support; these requirements have not yet been consolidated. We address this gap through meta-requirements: higher-order requirements specifying what a class of auditing frameworks should support. In design science research, literature and domain experts are common sources of meta-requirements; accordingly, we derive the initial set from literature and validate and refine it with practitioners. Our systematic literature review retained 74 of 2,890 records and derived 43 meta-requirements across 16 categories. We evaluated them with 128 practitioners, obtaining 5,504 ratings and 586 substantive comments. Overall, 81.20% of ratings indicated agreement or strong agreement. In particular, 41 of the 43 literature-derived meta-requirements were classified as strongly supported. Practitioner feedback refined the requirements and identified an additional requirement concerning external components and supply chain dependencies. The final set comprises 44 meta-requirements across 16 categories, of which 43 received quantitative validation. These meta-requirements can help organizations implement AI robustness auditing frameworks, assess existing frameworks for completeness, and refine them.

AI.brief_summary: 通过系统性文献综述与 128 名从业者评分，提炼并验证 AI 鲁棒性审计框架应支持的 44 条元需求（16 类），用于评估现有审计框架的完备性。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文属 AI 鲁棒性审计的需求工程研究，不涉及视觉或多模态推理的表示、latent 状态生成与使用，仅「证据是否足以支持结论」在抽象层面与推理中的证据充分性判断略有相似，不足以构成可核查的借鉴线索。
